primary_source_receipts.finding: The filing states Bitcoin traded above $126,000 in 2025 and fell from above $126,000 to below $81,000 between October and November 2025. It supports the approximate peak, not the transcript's full endpoint series or source timestamp.

IBIT reported that U.S. spot Bitcoin products experienced their largest quarterly net outflows since launch in Q2 2026. The filing does not reproduce exact June aggregate outflows, a 79% IBIT share or 45% weekly-price explanatory power.

Strategy stated that its June 29 program could generate up to $1.25 billion for the USD Reserve and that the full capacity remained available as of July 5. This was authorization, not a completed 20,000-coin sale.

MARA reported about $1.5 billion of Q1 Bitcoin sales used to retire debt and reduce a credit line. It supports liquidity-driven selling by one large miner, not the transcript's industry-wide 32,000-BTC total.

The probability-based SHED of nearly 13,000 adults reports 10% used cryptocurrency for investment or transactions in 2025. The report warns its online sample may be more technologically connected; the measure is prior-year use, not all-time ownership.
BIP-360 is a draft Pay-to-Merkle-Root proposal in the BIP repository. Repository acceptance is not Bitcoin Core activation, and the proposal does not prove quantum timing.

BIP-361 is a draft describing phased migration, restrictions and proposed rescue protocols. It cites more than 34% of bitcoin with revealed public keys but is not adopted code or a settled plan to confiscate one-third of supply.
The subsidy begins at 50 BTC and halves every 210,000 blocks. From 3.125 BTC, three further halvings yield 0.390625 BTC, one eighth; timing around 2036 remains block-dependent.
